minutes.headline: Assessors approved a backlog of 2023 minutes with corrections, set Monday meetings, then went into executive session.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors spent the first part of the meeting working through a backlog of prior minutes, amending several to fix attendance and nomination wording. It set a first-and-third-Monday meeting schedule, discussed a tax-bill insert and outreach to seniors and veterans, and heard the interim principal assessor's report on new construction. Discussion of contracts, the revaluation and future agenda items followed, and the board ended by entering executive session under purpose 7, not to return to open session.

public_comment.topic: A resident said the board should communicate through a well-informed website page and town notifications.
A resident raised concern that the Vision cards carry a site index (size adjustment) increase well above what the abatements produced, and that it will flow into future bills.
A resident said that in outsourcing contracts the RFP scope of services is where the board should be most involved.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors ended the meeting by entering executive session under purpose 7, and did not return to open session.
The board worked through a backlog of prior minutes and amended several to correct attendance and nomination wording.
Meetings were tentatively set for the first and third Mondays at 6:30 through December, starting November 6.
A member was nominated to work with the town manager on the Q3 tax-bill insert; the vote passed.
The interim principal assessor reported new construction, and the board agreed to audit building permits against what was captured; two land withdrawal notices were tabled.

why_it_matters: The tax-bill insert and the permit audit touch what residents see in their bills and whether new construction is fully counted in assessed value.

A resident raised the Vision cards' size-adjustment increases at public comment; the minutes do not show whether the board acted on it, and the revaluation and Vision contract discussion is largely garbled in the captions.
watch_next: Board meeting on November 6, when the board hopes to have Nate attend and has the first of the tentatively set Monday meetings.
The purchase and sales agreements that would allow the tabled land withdrawal notices to return to the agenda.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the mileage approval and the meeting schedule, but disagree on most of the votes. Ours mostly has votes "not audible", and the official minutes describe different motions. A reader should know that the insert/outreach motions and the tabled item (Chapter land withdrawals vs Lake Group) need checking against the recording, and that ours has several items (dollar figures, building-permit audit, Nate) that the official minutes lack.
